findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the backside of the ice machine baffles to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The PIC covered the ice and sanitized the baffles. Discussed increasing the frequency of cleaning during summer months. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of consumables.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to initially be dispensing 10 ppm. CORRECTED-the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm chlorine after the machine was primed and chemicals were refreshed. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently tested to verify proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed foods in the salad prep cooler to have internal temperatures ranging from 46-57F. CORRECTED- items were moved under time as control. Foods that are not used will be discarded at the end of service (the facility is open for 4 hours at a time). Ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used or discarded within 4 hours when out of temperature control (below 41F and above 135F respectively).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the salad prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. For temperatures within the cooler, reference violation 22. The ladles were replaced with ones with shorter handles, allowing the top to close more completely. Items cooled significantly in a 30 minute time period.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to initially be dispensing 0 ppm. Staff stated they had run the dish machine multiple times beforehand- and were therefore unaware of improper sanitizing concentrations. CORRECTED- the dish machine was run again and observed to be dispensing 50 ppm chlorine. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently tested to verify proper sanitizing concentration per manufacturer's label.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple house made sauces in the walk in cooler to be held past the seven day date marking period (3/6). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the sauces to be discarded and remade. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used to discarded within seven days. The date of preparation, thawing, opening, etc. counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hinge lid on the salad prep cooler to be loose from its fitting. CORRECTED- the PIC reset the screws during the inspection. Ensure all equipment is maintained in proper repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plates at the sushi station and in the kitchen to be face up. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved some of the plates underneath the counter at the kitchen, and inverted those that didn’t fit. Plates at the sushi station were moved to a lower rack, so that they could be under a cover. Ensure this practice continues to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple-door prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. All items in prep cooler were probed and voluntarily thrown away. Items probed include: Raw Pork (49.5 F), Cooked Pasta (47.5 F), Raw Steak (47F), Raw Lobster Tail (47F), Raw Salmon (46F), and a house made sauce (47F). PIC stated that all items were stored in the cooler last night, which exceeds the 6 hour time allotment that foods can be between 46-55F. Food is likely out of temperature due to a faulty cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC has scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Inspector will return 05/20/2025 to re-asses violation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the 3-door prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. Discussed with PIC and PIC has maintenance scheduled for the cooler. For temperatures within the cooler, reference violation 22. Inspector will return 05/22/2025 to reassess violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed salmon being thawed in reduced oxygen packaging in two coolers in the kitchen. The packaging bears a sticker that says to thaw outside of the package. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that fish is thawed according to packaging guidelines. Inspector will return 05/23/2025 to reassess violation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the active CFPM in the facility to not have an allergen training. The facility has multiple certified CFPMs with allergen trainings. Ensure that the active CFPM in the establishment has an allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine was observed with no measurable Cl concentration. PIC called GFS for service. The 3 compartment sink will be used to wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes until the dish machine is functional and dispensing 50-200ppm Cl in the sanitizing rinse.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a minimum concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) Foods in the countertop cooler were observed above 41F when probed (ketchup at 48F; sliced tomato at 54F; cheese at 50F; dressings at 52F and 54F). 
2) Foods in the shorter cookline prep cooler were observed above 41F when probed (raw chicken at 51F; raw beef at 47F).
CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure TCS food are held at 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The countertop cooler and short cookline prep cooler are not holding foods at 41F or below. PIC will call for maintenance on both coolers. Ensure all cold holding units are functioning and able to hold foods at or below 41F.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: ROP fish was observed stored in sealed packages that bear labels indicating that fish must be removed from ROP before thawing. Thaw ROP fish according to packaging.
